rows.grounds: compound of mahā (great) and vidyā (knowledge/mantra); subject of the verse
negative compound a-nādyā; qualifies mahāvidyā as without beginning
compound viśada (clear) + sukha (bliss) + da (giving); qualifies pade
relative pronoun introducing the state bestowed
verb expressing the bestowal effected by mahāvidyā
locative noun denoting the supreme abode or condition

items.question: What supreme state does the beginningless great knowledge bestow upon the seeker?
premises: This beginningless great knowledge has the power to grant a state.
The state granted is characterized by clear bliss.
items.inference: Therefore, the beginningless great knowledge bestows the state of clear bliss.
uncertainties: The precise verbal root and form of chatu are uncertain in this context.
items.plain_english: May the beginningless great knowledge grant that state which gives clear bliss.
